# Studienstiftung Overview
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, initially founded in Dresden in 1925 and re-established in Cologne in 1948, is a prestigious German scholarship foundation that provides financial and academic support to exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates. Admission is competitive and occurs through several channels including nomination by high schools, university professors, examination boards, winners of national competitions, and through assessment tests. Scholarships require full-time enrollment at universities either in Germany, another EU country, or Switzerland, and accept applicants regardless of citizenship or age.
Financial support typically includes a monthly allowance and subsidies for insurance, with need-based scholarships offering up to €855 monthly; doctoral scholars receive higher monthly awards. Academic support consists of summer schools, research groups, language courses, workshops, and mentoring. The foundation also offers internal and open scholarship programs in cooperation with other organizations. As of 2023, approximately 14,888 scholars were supported annually. The Studienstiftung boasts notable alumni across natural sciences, social sciences, business, politics, arts, and journalism, including Nobel laureates and leading academics.
